newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong handover to underpin property market - JLW.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong handover to underpin property market - JLW.

text.p: Positive sentiment surrounding Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule should buoy activity in the territory's property market in the short term while economic growth should stimulate it longer term, Jones Lang Wootton said.
In its Asia Pacific Property report for 1997, the real estate consultancy said it expected 15 to 20 percent capital value growth in the luxury and mass residential markets in 1997.
In the office market, capital values of Grade A offices are forecast to climb by 15 to 20 percent while capital values of other grade offices are set to rise 10 to 15 percent, it added.
"Economic fundamentals for the property market are sound and all sectors of the market should further improve in 1997," Jones Lang Wootton said.

"Positive sentiment generated by the handover will underpin short term activities. In the longer term, stronger economic growth in both Hong Kong and China will stimulate demand for property in the territory," it said.
Britain hands Hong Kong back to China on midnight of June 30.
Jones Lang Wootton said continued low levels of supply and a general increase in affluence would underpin the residential market.

"The office market has improved considerably during 1996 with capital values climbing by an average of 42 percent. The outlook for 1997 is optimistic due to the expansion of many different types of business, for example the financial, telecommunications, and computer industries," it added.

Retail activity linked to an inflow of tourists expected for the handover is likely to boost demand for retail space, Jones Lang Wootton said. "The strong demand of prime rental locations will lead to a rental growth of 15-20 percent," it said.
In the industrial/office market, Jones Lang Wootton said it expected rents and values to grow by 20 percent in 1997.
